title.en: A funny toast for a friend
title.es: Un brindis gracioso para un amigo

es: Preparar un brindis de cumpleaños con bromas amables, una hipérbole con so/such y una revisión que elimina lo ofensivo.

teaching.en: A good toast opens with a generous word, so every joke that follows feels like friendship, not attack.
teaching.es: Un buen brindis empieza con una palabra generosa, así que cada broma que sigue se siente como amistad y no como ataque.
teaching.explanationEs: Empieza por lo cálido: el humor posterior se interpreta con ese tono.
segments: A good toast opens with a generous word, so
every joke that follows feels like friendship, not attack.
teaching.audioText: A good toast opens with a generous word, so every joke that follows feels like friendship, not attack.

teaching.en: Gentle teasing about small habits, such as arriving late to her own party, makes a speech warm, not rude.
teaching.es: Las bromas suaves sobre pequeños hábitos, como llegar tarde a su propia fiesta, hacen cálido un discurso y no grosero.
teaching.explanationEs: Bromea sobre hábitos inocentes que la persona pueda cambiar y reírse de ellos.
segments: Gentle teasing about small habits, such as arriving late to
her own party, makes a speech warm, not rude.
teaching.audioText: Gentle teasing about small habits, such as arriving late to her own party, makes a speech warm, not rude.

teaching.en: Jokes about age, money or looks are offensive, and an embarrassing story can make the whole room go silent.
teaching.es: Las bromas sobre la edad, el dinero o el aspecto son ofensivas, y una anécdota embarazosa puede dejar en silencio a toda la sala.
teaching.explanationEs: Temas prohibidos: edad, dinero, aspecto y cualquier cosa que avergüence.
segments: Jokes about age, money or looks are offensive, and an
embarrassing story can make the whole room go silent.
teaching.audioText: Jokes about age, money or looks are offensive, and an embarrassing story can make the whole room go silent.

teaching.en: When you revise a draft, ask whether any joke might cross the line between teasing and being rude.
teaching.es: Cuando revises un borrador, pregúntate si alguna broma podría pasarse de la raya entre bromear y ser grosero.
teaching.explanationEs: Revisar es parte del brindis: la línea entre cariño y ofensa es fina.
segments: When you revise a draft, ask whether any joke
might cross the line between teasing and being rude.
teaching.audioText: When you revise a draft, ask whether any joke might cross the line between teasing and being rude.

teaching.en: If a remark feels dangerous, tone down the exaggeration, keep the kindness and finish the speech with a sincere cheers.
teaching.es: Si un comentario parece peligroso, suaviza la exageración, conserva el cariño y termina el discurso con un sincero cheers.
teaching.explanationEs: Tone down: bajar la intensidad sin perder la intención amable.
segments: If a remark feels dangerous, tone down the exaggeration, keep
the kindness and finish the speech with a sincere cheers.
teaching.audioText: If a remark feels dangerous, tone down the exaggeration, keep the kindness and finish the speech with a sincere cheers.

teaching.en: A toast should go down well with everybody, so invite the guests to raise a glass only after the last kind word.
teaching.es: Un brindis debe ser bien recibido por todos, así que invita a los invitados a alzar la copa solo tras la última palabra amable.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre sincero y el gesto de brindar rematan el discurso.
segments: A toast should go down well with everybody, so invite the
guests to raise a glass only after the last kind word.
teaching.audioText: A toast should go down well with everybody, so invite the guests to raise a glass only after the last kind word.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador de Leo: ¿qué broma debería quitar?

choices.text: The joke about Tom's age.
The joke about the wedding cake.
The joke about the coffee.

feedback.es: Las bromas sobre hábitos (tarde, generoso) son cariñosas; la de la edad es el tema que más fácilmente ofende y conviene cortarla.

hint.es: Piensa en qué rasgo no puede cambiar Tom.

origin.text: Leo's draft for Tom's birthday has three jokes. First: Tom is so late that he arrived at his own wedding after the cake. Second: Tom is so old that his birthday candles need a fire permit. Third: Tom is so generous that he pays for everybody's coffee.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una broma sobre su edad se pasaría de la raya.»

feedback.es: Cross the line es la expresión fija para pasarse del límite entre la broma cariñosa y la ofensiva.

hint.es: Verbo que significa atravesar un límite.

origin.text: Mia loves jokes about her terrible map-reading, but a joke about her age would ___ the line. Her brother knows exactly where it is.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión del brindis con su función.

pairs.es: pasar del humor a la ofensa

feedback.es: Cada expresión marca un momento del brindis: bromear, suavizar, cerrar y evitar el exceso.

hint.es: Ordénalas mentalmente: primero bromeas, luego revisas, al final brindas.

pairs.es: pasar del humor a la ofensa

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué broma le pide su hermano que quite del brindis?

choices.text: The joke about how dangerous his cooking is.
The joke about how much money he makes.
The joke about losing his own birthday.

feedback.es: Se ríe de las bromas sobre su memoria y su cocina, pero pide que quite la del sueldo: es un tema personal que prefiere dejar fuera.

origin.audio: Mia read her draft toast to her brother. She had written that he was so forgetful that he once lost his own birthday, and that his cooking was such a danger to the neighbourhood that the firefighters knew his name. Her brother laughed, but he asked her to remove the line about his salary.

prompt.es: Lee la nota de la invitada: ¿qué opina del discurso?

choices.text: It was almost perfect, but too many jokes were about habits.
Part of it made some guests laugh but hurt another.
It was a success with all, including the grandmother.
It was almost perfect, but the grandmother should have laughed too.

feedback.es: Elogia el discurso («almost perfect»), pero señala que la broma sobre la edad hizo reír a los amigos y dejó incómoda a la abuela.

origin.text: Thanks for the speech, it was almost perfect. The joke about Tom's age got a big laugh from his friends, but his grandmother looked at her plate for the rest of the evening. Next time, perhaps we could keep the teasing for things that he can change.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Suaviza cualquier broma que pueda avergonzar al invitado.»

answer.text: Tone down any joke that might be embarrassing for the guest

feedback.es: Tone down lleva después el objeto (any joke) y una oración relativa que explica el riesgo.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato de la boda: ¿qué se deduce del silencio y de la reacción de la madre?

choices.text: That his mother disliked the earlier jokes as well as the last one.
That the speech ran long and the guests lost interest before the end.
That the line about the first wife crossed the line for the family.
That the best man had meant to upset the family on purpose.

feedback.es: Las bromas de hábitos funcionaron, pero la mención de la antigua novia provocó silencio y el gesto de la madre: esa línea fue la que se pasó de la raya.

origin.audio: At my cousin's wedding, the best man stood up with a card in one hand and a glass in the other. He began well: he said that my cousin was so generous that he had once given away his only umbrella in a storm, and so late for everything that his own wife had learned to tell him the wedding started an hour earlier. The guests laughed. Then he mentioned my cousin's first wife, and the room went quiet. My cousin's smile did not move, but his mother put down her glass. Afterwards the best man admitted that he had not read the room, and that one line had changed the whole evening.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le aconseja a Leo quien escribe el correo sobre su borrador?

choices.text: To delete the whole second page because it is too long for a toast.
To keep every joke, since Sara laughs at everything about herself.
To replace the cake joke with a more generous comment.
To keep the habit jokes and soften or cut the dress line.

feedback.es: Aprueba la broma del pastel porque Sara se ríe de ella, pero recomienda suavizar o eliminar la del vestido, que afecta algo que eligió con cuidado.

origin.text: Dear Leo, I have read your toast twice. The first page is lovely: the joke about Sara arriving after the cake is exactly the right kind of teasing, because she laughs at it herself. The second page worries me. The line about her dress might be funny to you, but I would tone it down, or leave it out, because she chose that dress with great care.

prompt.es: Completa: «Pidió a todos que alzaran una copa por la feliz pareja.»

feedback.es: Raise a glass es la expresión habitual para invitar a brindar al final de un discurso.

origin.text: After the last joke, the best man thanked the guests for their patience. Then he asked everybody to ___ a glass to the happy couple.

prompt.es: Escribe el brindis para Mia con bromas amables y una revisión (200–260 palabras).

answer.text: Friends and family, please raise a glass to Mia, who turns thirty today! Mia is so generous that she cooks dinner for the whole street, and she is so late for everything that she arrived at her own party after the cake. I am only joking: we would wait for her all night. She is kind of famous for her terrible maps, but she is such a good friend that we always follow her anyway. I had planned a joke about her age, but I have decided to cut it, because it could be embarrassing for her and it would not be fair. Instead, I want to say something sincere: thank you, Mia, for being the first person to call when things go wrong, and the last one to leave when they go right. We are lucky to have you. Cheers, Mia, and happy birthday!
accepted: Friends and family, please raise a glass to Mia, who turns thirty today! Mia is so generous that she cooks dinner for the whole street, and she is so late for everything that she arrived at her own party after the cake. I am only joking: we would wait for her all night. She is kind of famous for her terrible maps, but she is such a good friend that we always follow her anyway. I had planned a joke about her age, but I have decided to cut it, because it could be embarrassing for her and it would not be fair. Instead, I want to say something sincere: thank you, Mia, for being the first person to call when things go wrong, and the last one to leave when they go right. We are lucky to have you. Cheers, Mia, and happy birthday!

Dear friends, let us all raise a glass to Carlos on his fortieth birthday. He is so kind that he lends his car to anybody who asks, and he is so forgetful that he once looked for his phone while he was talking on it. I am just joking: we love him exactly as he is. Carlos is sort of a legend in the kitchen, but he is such a funny cook that we always eat before we arrive. I wrote a joke about his money, and I will not read it, because it would be unfair and it could hurt people who love him. Thank you, Carlos, for every good day, and for always being the first person to help when something goes wrong. Cheers to Carlos, and happy birthday!

feedback.es: Un brindis completo tiene bromas amables con so/such… that, un suavizador, la revisión visible de lo que se retira y un cierre sincero.

origin.text: Mia cumple 30 años. Es muy generosa, siempre llega tarde y se pierde con los mapas. Escribe en inglés un brindis: dos bromas amables con so/such… that, un suavizador (kind of, only joking), una broma sobre su edad que decides quitar y un cierre sincero con cheers.

evidenceGroups: i will not make a joke
i would not make a joke

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe esta columna quien firma el texto?

choices.text: To persuade speakers to cut any joke that they are unsure about.
To suggest that speakers should always read their jokes to their mothers.
To explain how to write the funniest lines for a speech.
To ban all jokes in speeches given at family parties.

feedback.es: Su regla es práctica: ante la duda, corta; el criterio de «repetirlo ante su madre» sirve para decidir, no prohíbe el humor.

origin.text: Nobody has ever been sorry that they cut a dangerous joke. Many have been sorry that they kept one. When in doubt, ask yourself whether the person being teased would repeat the line to her mother. If not, it probably does not belong in the speech, however well it sounds in your head.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por favor, alza la copa por mi generoso amigo.»

answer.text: Please raise a glass to my generous friend

feedback.es: Raise a glass to + persona es la fórmula para invitar al brindis; el adjetivo generous va antes del nombre.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Mia: ¿qué actitud muestra ante el brindis de Leo?

choices.text: She is happy with the whole speech and says he should repeat it exactly.
She is pleased overall but asks him to cut the joke that embarrassed others.
She is upset by the age joke and will only forgive him after an apology.
She agrees with her aunt that the joke about the maps went too far.

feedback.es: Celebra la broma sobre los mapas, pero pide quitar la de su edad, que incomodó a otros: aprueba el tono general y corrige un punto.

origin.audio: Hi Leo, it is Mia. I listened to the recording of your toast. The part about my terrible maps made everybody laugh, and I loved it. The part about my age, on the other hand, made my aunt stare at her plate. Please leave that one out next time, and I will forgive you completely.
